title: Parking schema in PostgreSQL
idea: The parking schema maps the Java model to tables so PostgreSQL enforces the core rule itself: at most one open ticket per spot and per plate.

analogy.text: A key cabinet with one hook per bay. A clerk takes the first key nobody is reaching for, so two clerks never hand out the same bay.
analogy.breaks: Taken hooks here are skipped silently, not queued for.

points: Partial unique indexes allow one open ticket per spot and per plate.
`CHECK` constraints keep enum values legal and tie EXITED to an exit time.
`spot_free_idx` holds only FREE rows, keyed by type, floor and id.
Entry locks one free spot with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, so gates never queue.

steps.caption: Three cars arrive at once. Only F1-C1 and F2-C1 are FREE for cars.
IN-1 runs the allocation query and locks the first free row, F1-C1.
IN-2 runs the same query. `SKIP LOCKED` passes over F1-C1 and locks F2-C1.
IN-3 skips both locked rows and finds nothing. It answers LOT_FULL at once.
IN-1 and IN-2 mark their spots OCCUPIED, insert tickets and commit.
Without `SKIP LOCKED`, IN-2 and IN-3 would wait for IN-1's lock first.

code.title: Tables and constraints
code.caption: The schema on a real PostgreSQL 18, then six bad writes the database refuses by itself.

walk.text: Fixed layout: floors and spots. Enums are TEXT with a CHECK.
Partial index of FREE spots by type, floor and id; one type's lookup reads floor order.
`ticket` ties a plate to a spot; named checks link status and exit time.
Partial unique indexes: one open ticket per spot and per plate.
`payment` keeps money as BIGINT paise and makes the Idempotency-Key unique.
Each bad write prints the Postgres error code and the constraint that stopped it.
After T-1 exits, F1-C1 accepts a new car: the partial index released it.

code.title: The entry transaction
code.caption: Three gates race for two free compact spots, then a paid exit frees one. It uses trimmed tables so the race stays short.

walk.text: `tx` runs one function inside BEGIN and COMMIT, and rolls back on error.
Lock the first free fitting spot: smallest type, lowest floor, skipping locked rows.
No row means LOT_FULL; otherwise occupy the spot and insert the ticket.
Exit only a PAID ticket, then free its spot in the same transaction.
Three parallel entries; print the sorted results, never who won.
A truck finds no LARGE spot; F1-C1 leaves only after paying; the next car gets it.
All three spots end OCCUPIED; one_car_per_spot guarantees one open ticket each.

pitfalls: Forgetting `WHERE status <> 'EXITED'` makes the unique index block every later visit.
Update ticket and spot in one transaction, or a crash leaves a spot stuck OCCUPIED.
Use `SKIP LOCKED` only when any free row will do, never for one chosen seat.

quiz.q: What does enter.mjs print for the three gates?
quiz.why: Each gate locks a different FREE row or skips it. F1-L1 is already OCCUPIED, so the third gate finds no row and returns LOT_FULL.

takeaway: Let partial unique indexes and row locks decide who gets each spot.

starters: Why keep a status column on parking_spot when tickets already show occupancy?
When is SKIP LOCKED the wrong tool?
